name.text: Permutations in Real Life 4 - Match the scenario to the formula (matching)

questiontext.text: Match each real-life situation to the calculation that gives the number of possible arrangements. Order matters in every situation.

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution

Ask two questions: Are all the items being arranged, or only some of them? and Is any position fixed?

All items arranged: use \(n!\). Seven students in a row give \(7! = 5040\).

Only some items arranged: use \(_nP_r = \dfrac{n!}{(n-r)!}\). A 4-digit code from 10 digits gives \(_{10}P_4 = 5040\).

One position fixed: arrange the rest, \((n-1)!\). With the captain batting last, the other 8 players give \(8! = 40\,320\).

Two groups chosen together: multiply the counts. A plate with 3 letters and 3 digits gives \(_{26}P_3 \times {}_{10}P_3\).

subquestion.text: A phone uses a 4-digit code made from different digits 0 to 9.
First, second and third prizes are awarded among 20 contestants.
Seven students stand in a single row for a class photo.
A team of 9 players needs a batting order, and the captain must bat last.
A number plate has 3 different letters followed by 3 different digits.
A playlist of 5 songs is made from 15 songs, and the order matters.
